text:
oliver: heads-up — running HF jinja chat_template -> Redwood conversion for the new quantized llama2 snapshot and seeing sentinel tokens split across token boundaries.

maya: ugh. any repro steps? :thinking:

oliver: minimal repro attached below. jinja block:```
{% for msg in chat %}
{{ msg.role }}: {{ msg.content }}
{% endfor %}
```converted prompt contains our sentinel `<|system|>` but tokenizer ends up as `['<', '|system', '|>']` on the fast tokenizer.

jordan: can you paste the tokenizer.tokenize output?

oliver: sure — run:```py
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/llama2-quant-test', use_fast=True)
print(t.tokenize('<|system|> hello'))
```gives: `['<', '|system', '|>', 'Ġhello']` (notice the split).

maya: that's the problem — Redwood convert expects the sentinel to be a single atomic token (we render role prefixes as single-token sentinels). if it splits, the renderer insertion/truncation logic can chop the middle and produce role-bleed.

oliver: right — observed this in evals: conv_adherence dropped from 0.92 -> 0.64 on the new quant checkpoint. failing cases show assistant ignoring system instructions because the sentinels are no longer preserved.

jordan: quick options: add the sentinel to tokenizer.special_tokens (e.g., `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': ['<|system|>']})`) and save that tokenizer, or use non-fast tokenizer which sometimes preserves. downside: some tokenizers still byte-split on normalization.

dev-ex: another approach: conversion script can detect when a sentinel splits and replace it with a private-use placeholder before tokenization, then stitch back after rendering. eg replace `<|system|>` -> `1SYS2` during conversion, add sanitizer. downside: hacks increase surface area for bugs.

oliver: tried add_special_tokens and re-saved tokenizer, but CI with quantized model still produced splits inside the fast tokenizer for certain unicode-normalized builds. suspect difference in tokenizers between upstream HF and our local build used during quantization.

maya: is it possible quantization pipeline (bitsandbytes/gptq) changed tokenizer metadata when we repacked weights? shouldn't, but we saw mismatches before when packaging model + tokenizer together.

jordan: checklist for next steps: 1) ensure tokenizer files (tokenizer.json, special_tokens_map.json) are bundled with the model artifact used by Redwood convert; 2) conversion should validate that each sentinel token tokenizes to exactly one token and fail early otherwise; 3) add unit test in eng-ml/tests/conv that runs tokenizer.tokenize on the canonical sentinels.

oliver: I'll open a PR that runs the single-token assertion in the conversion step and emits a clear error pointing to tokenizer files. will add a fallback that attempts `tokenizer.add_special_tokens(...)` and repack if safe.

maya: add an eval job to run the conv_adherence harness after conversion — we need automated guardrails. also capture the failing prompt examples. :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: deploy pipeline: conversion-pr-oliver66 passed unit checks, integration pending.

jordan: one more gotcha we hit: some Jinja macros inject whitespace or zero-width spaces which, combined with tokenizer normalization, cause the sentinel to be split after trimming. final suggestion: normalize the jinja pre-render to collapse adjunct zero-width chars and guarantee sentinel sits on ASCII boundaries (or escape with a delimiter token e.g. `<<SYS_START>>`).

oliver: noted. for now PR will: validate tokenization, try add_special_tokens fallback, and emit example tokenization diffs in the error. maya will add the evaluation job. jordan will try the private-use placeholder prototype if we need a hotfix.

dev-ex: thanks — this explains a weird regression we couldn't track in quant experiments. keep thread updated with PR links. :eyes:

oliver: will post PR link when ready, and add the failing eval dump.

maya: thanks all.
